explanation: Working in Szeged, a paprika-growing city, he found that the local peppers were packed with vitamin C. He received the 1937 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

claims.text: Szent-Györgyi extracted vitamin C in large quantities from Hungarian paprika peppers.
Szent-Györgyi's bulk source of vitamin C was paprika, not sour cherries, apricots or walnuts.
Albert Szent-Györgyi was awarded the 1937 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, for discoveries that included work on vitamin C.
Szent-Györgyi did this work at Szeged, a city in a region known for growing paprika.
